title: Architecture
text:
Components 
           Component Responsibility 
             AgentBrain Conversational Agents SDK manager; owns objectives, priorities and mandatory criteria. 
             Supervisor One process owner, serialized decisions, asynchronous workers and independent heartbeat. 
             Store ,  Control SQLite goals, revisions, conversations, messages, ownership and result fences. 
             Research ,  Knowledge Discovery, hypotheses, captured evidence, independent evaluation and retrieval. 
             Implementations Explicit authorization, isolated Git worktrees, executable checks, bounded repair and audit. 
             CodexRuntime Real App Server sessions; the original Node SDK bridge remains available. 
             dashboard ,  web_auth HTML application, scoped goal creation, password sessions and durable inbox controls. 
           
           Python, OpenAI Agents SDK and SQLite. No workflow framework, broker, automatic merge or application deployment. 
           Context and control 
           SQLiteSession('manager:<goal-id>')  retains manager conversation in the adjacent sessions DB. The latest 12 session items and task summaries bound prompt context; worker histories remain separate. Goals, original criteria, decisions and knowledge survive restarts. 
           A process lock enforces one owner per database. An async actor lock serializes decisions; durable inbox messages reach that owner without starting another. Waiting dependencies do not poll a model. Deadlines and reasoning budgets pause work. 
           Policy and requirement changes require explicit acceptance. Review shows old/new instructions, added criteria, affected tasks and approval/evidence effects. Each proposal binds its original goal/policy revisions; stale proposals cannot apply. Mandatory originals remain. Task generations reject affected late results, while unaffected work remains available. 
           Research and knowledge 
           Stage Bounded contract 
             Discovery At most 20 explicit sources; map resources and rank opportunities. 
             Focused research At most 8 sources; one falsifiable hypothesis, contradictory evidence and an execution budget. 
             Evaluation Inspect captured evidence independently; support, falsify, request targeted evidence or block. 
             Manager Resolve the highest-value uncertainty; retry with feedback, replan or stop. 
           
           Research reads scoped local UTF-8 exports: 32 MiB per file, 1–100 lines per call. Knowledge prefetch preserves discretionary read budget. DB-backed SDK tools are async. Reports return directly to the manager. 
           Evidence records excerpts, source hashes and timestamps. Citation gates reject missing or stale citations; an LLM cannot establish truth by assertion. Independently supported claims become verified. Discovery maps and findings publish atomically with a final goal/policy revision check under a SQLite writer lock. 
           Exact question/scope/source signatures detect repeat investigations. Changed sources and aged logs/metrics flag stale knowledge. Time, tool, turn and attempt caps persist; exhausted budgets escalate. These mechanisms do not detect every paraphrase or guarantee good research judgment. 
           Coding and verification 
           
             User authorization binds accepted research, goal/policy revisions, allowed paths, checks and attempt limits. Every mandatory criterion needs an executable check. 
             Real Codex edits an isolated worktree. Candidate SHA, artifacts, concerns and questions persist. No automatic merge or deployment follows. 
             Independent subprocesses execute authorized checks in a clean worktree at that exact candidate. Outputs, digests, exit codes and revision coverage persist. 
             Local defects receive bounded repair. Incorrect assumptions return to research; repeated failures require a changed approach. 
             A goal audit compares the candidate against every current criterion. A worker success claim cannot complete a code goal. 
           
           The UI checklist requires current authorization, goal/policy revisions and candidate SHA. One passing assertion cannot hide another failing check for that criterion; whole-goal verification requires one implementation covering all criteria. Trusted test commands are not a hostile-code sandbox. 
           Codex and delivery 
           OPENAI_API_KEY  configures the Responses provider through  env_key ; its value is never persisted by the adapters. Session IDs and a writable Codex home survive application restarts. 
           Native thread start/resume/read and turn start/steer/interrupt APIs preserve real runtime identity. Steering uses expected-turn preconditions. Old connection-specific question IDs cannot be replayed after reconnect. 
           Delivery distinguishes pending, sending, acknowledged, uncertain and  sent_no_ack . RPC acceptance does not establish task completion. Unknown outcomes require reconciliation before retry; SDK research restarts as a fresh bounded attempt. 
           Recovery and observation 
           A separate heartbeat continues during slow manager replies. Online requires both a held owner lock and a recent heartbeat; a held lock with an old heartbeat is stale. Clean shutdown records stopped state. Worker activity and tokens do not count as meaningful progress. 
           Dashboard snapshots use read-only transactions. Authenticated commands append to the durable inbox. Goal creation validates an existing workspace inside the configured root, preserves original criteria and is idempotent; it neither starts an owner nor authorizes code changes. 
           Password login uses scrypt hashes, persistent revocable sessions, secure HttpOnly cookies behind HTTPS, origin checks and CSRF tokens for writes. Optional bearer access remains available. The UI separates live, recorded, stale and offline state and retains its last snapshot after connection failures. 
           Single-host service templates  provide persistent paths and an HTTPS proxy. They are tested locally, not publicly deployed. GitHub Pages serves archived experiment snapshots. See  recovery  for uncertain actions and backups.

title: Research campaigns
text:
Campaigns investigate a pinned local Git checkout using bounded discovery, hypothesis testing and fresh independent evaluation. They can remain active for days, with saved limits and an unexplored source catalog. The current Kafka investigation is an experiment; a multi-day reliability result has not been established. 
 Limits and money 
 The first invocation requires  --days  (up to 30),  --decisions ,  --research-runs  and  --dollars  (no greater than 25). Resume the same DB/goal without those flags. Saved deadline, consumed decisions, role attempts and dollar reservations do not reset. 
 All campaign manager/research/evaluation calls use the pinned  gpt-4.1-2025-04-14  model and standard service tier. The ledger uses the  official GPT-4.1 rates : $2 per million input tokens, $0.50 cached input, $8 output. Provider input-token counting includes the exact inline request and tool/schema definitions. Maximum output is 3,500 tokens. Maximum cost is reserved atomically before each paid request; actual usage releases the unused amount. Review these rates if provider pricing changes. 
 HTTP retries are disabled. A timeout, crash or lost response can have been billed: its full reservation stays held. The ledger may therefore stop below the cap. It excludes hosted tools, native Codex workers and other models, so those routes cannot create unaccounted campaign charges. Independent jobs using the same API account are outside this goal's ledger. 
 Large repositories and evidence 
 A streamed Git inventory builds a SQLite path catalog, with keyset pagination, component buckets and observed/unexamined counts. Full histories stay on disk; bounded manager state and recall tools prevent replaying the entire investigation. Excerpts and source counts describe observations, not exhaustive repository coverage. 
 omnitrix --db state.db campaign GOAL_ID --prepare-only \
  --evidence build/observations/context.txt \
  --evidence build/observations/service.log \
  --evidence build/observations/measurements.csv 
 Evidence paths must be existing UTF-8 files within the goal workspace, at most 32 MiB. Register exports explicitly; they retain a separate origin from tracked Git source. Record provenance, workload, units, measurement window, environment and limitations. Partition larger data. A local unit-test duration does not establish Kafka broker latency or production throughput. 
 Recovery and stopping 
 omnitrix --db state.db campaign GOAL_ID
omnitrix --db state.db campaign GOAL_ID --pause
# After diagnosing a deliberate pause or false early completion:
omnitrix --db state.db campaign GOAL_ID --continue-paused 
 One owner holds the DB lock. Read-only SDK interruptions retain evidence and charged attempts; uncertain requests keep their cost reservations. Explicit continuation records the previous stop and resets only the stagnation window. Crashes and ordinary resumes preserve it. It does not authorize resetting limits or replaying native actions. 
 Deadline, decision, role-run and dollar exhaustion stop work. Eight decisions without new source access pause the owner; new workers get their bounded chance to read before the stagnation check. Investigate the failure before continuing. The process needs a surviving host or an external process supervisor; no cloud scheduler or machine-to-machine recovery is included. 
 Default completion minima require 20 observed files, 4 component buckets, 6 independently resolved hypotheses and 2 verified code mechanism findings. A mechanism needs a workload and falsification condition. Evidence gaps and measurements have separate categories. These gates prevent trivial data-gap completion but do not prove correctness or prevent every semantic reviewer error. Do not invent issues to satisfy them; budget/deadline exhaustion may produce an honest incomplete or negative result. 
 Longitudinal tracking 
 research-quality.html  is generated from  docs/research-quality.json . Each issue has its original diagnosis, current status, and dated observations, changes, tests and regressions. Experiment summaries keep their earlier timestamped versions. Model outcomes remain separate from deterministic guard tests and manual validation. 
 Campaign HTML checkpoints are replaced atomically every minute and on exit. The SQLite history and exported report include decisions, research queries/evidence, evaluations, inventory queries, challenges, recovery events and a per-request spending ledger. Preserve the DB and any  .sessions.db  sidecar with their WAL state before moving machines; keep the pinned checkout and exported evidence. 
 Current experiment boundary 
 Kafka is pinned at  cc8baadc9f0363f2bdfe68a2f1cd8dbe4372d282 , with 7,545 indexed tracked text files and six explicitly registered local validation exports. The saved run has a 72-hour deadline, 1,000 decisions, 2,000 role runs and a $25 cap. It performs no external publication or source edits. 
 Live testing reproduced premature completion, repeated invalid plans and a false inference about JMH instrumentation. The prior accepted claim was challenged and downgraded; original reports remain. Navigation, controller instructions and completion checks have changed, but autonomous research quality remains under evaluation. A manually prepared Kafka LRU cache baseline passed three unit tests; that is environment validation, not an agent-discovered inefficiency or measured optimization.

title: Mission control
text:
Start locally 
 omnitrix dashboard-user operator --users .omnitrix/auth/users.json
omnitrix --db .omnitrix/state.db dashboard --allow-control \
  --auth-users .omnitrix/auth/users.json --workspace-root .
# Separate owner process, initially waiting for commands:
omnitrix --db .omnitrix/state.db run GOAL_ID --steps 0 --hours 4 
 The default bind is loopback port 8765. Sign in with the account you created. Passwords are hashed;
browser sessions use revocable HttpOnly cookies and CSRF protection. Resetting a password invalidates
its sessions. Public HTTPS needs the  single-host deployment . 
 What to inspect 
 View Meaning 
 Overview Current objective, manager heartbeat, original and added criteria, exact-revision verification and final audit. 
 Manager chat Send messages, steer/pause/cancel tasks, run bounded decisions and review instruction changes. 
 Tasks Inspect hypothesis, scope, budget, findings, contradictions, blockers, source evidence and checks. 
 Hierarchy Actual manager assignments. Evaluators and test processes are identified separately. 
 Knowledge Recorded findings and classifications. Revalidate sources before reusing them. 
 Activity Decisions, progress and durable message receipts. 
 
 Control and approval 
 Create goals with mandatory criteria and an existing workspace inside the configured root.
Code goals require a committed repository; creation grants no coding permission and starts no owner.
One manager owns each database. The UI marks goals without an owner offline. 
 Policy replaces the complete instruction text; requirements add constraints and mandatory criteria.
Review old/new text, affected tasks, evidence and approvals before accepting. A stale proposal requires
new review. Code authorization stays explicit in the CLI; no deployment command is exposed. 
 Delivery and liveness 
 State Interpretation 
 Queued / processing Durable request awaiting or being handled by the manager. 
 Acknowledged Receipt handled; this does not mean the engineering goal succeeded. 
 Answered / failed Recorded response or error, linked to the request. 
 Uncertain Inspect state before resending. An unchanged retry reuses its request ID. 
 Online / stale / offline Owner lock plus recent heartbeat, an old heartbeat, or no current owner. 
 
 State refreshes every five seconds. Disconnection retains the last snapshot and disables writes.
A heartbeat proves responsiveness, not worker progress. Snapshots are read-only; their timestamps and
experiment origin stay visible. 
 GitHub Pages 
 Pages shows three recorded real-model experiment runs. It cannot run the manager. Connect an
explicitly allowed HTTPS backend using the optional bearer-token flow; same-origin password login is
preferred on the actual backend site. Tokens are never stored in browser storage or published files. 
 Boundaries and checks 
 Recent-state reads are bounded to 200 goals and 200 records per category. Use CLI export for history.
Reads use one read-only transaction; writes use the durable inbox. Source changes, goal/policy revisions
and exact candidate SHAs constrain evidence. Executable checks and goal audit remain distinct. 
 pip install -e '.[test,docs,browser]'
python scripts/check_ui.py --chromium /usr/bin/chromium
python scripts/build_docs.py --check 
 Browser checks call no models. Rebuild README HTML and search with  python scripts/build_docs.py .
Only README is Markdown; other guides are maintained as HTML.

title: Deployment
text:
Request and execution paths Browser HTTPS and secure session cookie Caddy Automatic TLS → loopback port 8765 Dashboard Authenticated state and durable commands Manager owner Bounded agents; retained SQLite and sessions 
       Prepare the host 
       Use a supported Linux host with systemd, Python 3.11+, Node, Git and Caddy. Point your domain at it and allow inbound TCP 80/443. Keep port 8765 on loopback. 
       sudo useradd --system --home-dir /var/lib/omnitrix --shell /usr/sbin/nologin omnitrix
sudo git clone https://github.com/jinit24/omnitrix.git /opt/omnitrix
sudo python3 -m venv /opt/omnitrix/.venv
sudo /opt/omnitrix/.venv/bin/pip install -e /opt/omnitrix
sudo npm --prefix /opt/omnitrix ci
sudo install -d -o omnitrix -g omnitrix -m 0700 /var/lib/omnitrix/{auth,workspaces,codex}
sudo install -m 0600 /opt/omnitrix/deploy/omnitrix.env.example /etc/omnitrix.env
sudoedit /etc/omnitrix.env 
       Set  OPENAI_API_KEY  in that root-readable environment file. Paths may be configured there; writable state must remain under  /var/lib/omnitrix  unless the service's  ReadWritePaths  is updated too. Source code and dependencies remain outside worker workspaces. 
       Create a login and configure HTTPS 
       sudo -u omnitrix /opt/omnitrix/.venv/bin/python -m omnitrix.cli dashboard-user operator --users /var/lib/omnitrix/auth/users.json
sudo install -m 0644 /opt/omnitrix/deploy/Caddyfile /etc/caddy/Caddyfile
sudo install -d /etc/systemd/system/caddy.service.d
sudo install -m 0644 /opt/omnitrix/deploy/caddy.service.d/omnitrix.conf /etc/systemd/system/caddy.service.d/omnitrix.conf
sudo install -m 0600 /opt/omnitrix/deploy/caddy.env.example /etc/caddy/omnitrix.env
sudoedit /etc/caddy/omnitrix.env 
       Set  OMNITRIX_DOMAIN  to your DNS name without a scheme or path. The proxy receives only this domain setting; the dashboard service removes provider credentials from its environment. Reuse an existing Caddy configuration instead of overwriting it when the host serves other sites. 
       Validate and start 
       cd /opt/omnitrix
./deploy/check.sh
sudo install -m 0644 deploy/omnitrix-dashboard.service deploy/omnitrix-manager@.service /etc/systemd/system/
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo sh -c '. /etc/caddy/omnitrix.env; export OMNITRIX_DOMAIN; caddy validate --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile --adapter caddyfile'
sudo systemctl enable --now omnitrix-dashboard
sudo systemctl restart caddy 
       Open your HTTPS domain and sign in. Create a goal whose workspace is an existing directory under the configured root. A code goal requires a committed Git repository root. Creating a goal does not authorize code changes or start a manager. 
       sudo systemctl enable --now omnitrix-manager@GOAL_ID
sudo journalctl -u omnitrix-dashboard -u omnitrix-manager@GOAL_ID -f 
       Replace  GOAL_ID  with the created ID. Run only one manager service for this database. An exclusive lock rejects a second owner. The manager starts in standby with zero decisions; use the dashboard's bounded Continue control when ready. 
       Restart and restore 
       Event Behavior 
         Process failure systemd restarts it after five seconds; repeated startup failures stop after three attempts. 
         Manager restart Starts in standby. Running work and ambiguous sends require reconciliation before another autonomous action. 
         Service shutdown SIGINT allows manager cleanup; systemd terminates remaining processes after 45 seconds. 
         Disk persistence Retains state DB, adjacent conversation DB, worktrees, artifacts, auth sessions and Codex home. 
       
       Back up  /var/lib/omnitrix , the environment files and source revisions. Stop both application services for a consistent full-directory backup; copying an active SQLite file without its WAL is insufficient. Follow  recovery  before replacing uncertain work. No template merges code or deploys applications. 
       Validated here: systemd unit syntax, CLI flags, and Caddy 2.11.7 configuration. The official Caddy download matched its published SHA-512 checksum. A local HTTPS test verified secure login, CSRF-protected goal creation and logout using a temporary CA trusted only by the test client: 
       .venv/bin/python deploy/check_https.py --caddy /path/to/verified/caddy 
       Public DNS, certificate issuance, host-specific Codex sandbox execution and restart recovery still need validation on the selected host. No public deployment is claimed.

title: Experiments & results
text:
Measured results 
           Latest full development trial · fixture v2 · three paired tasks System Criteria Tasks Time Observed input / output tokens 
             Single Codex 6/6 3/3 58.217s 279,426 / 3,965 
             Manager 4/6 2/3 206.375s 532,213 / 13,928 
           
           GPT-5.4 coordinated research/evaluation; GPT-5.3-Codex workers used medium reasoning. Each pair received identical initial trees, unchanged executable criteria and a 420s cap. Both arms recorded zero incorrect completion claims. 
           No measured architecture advantage.  The manager completed deduplication and batching. Its retry hypothesis combined a real timeout defect with permanent-error behavior that already worked; after independent falsification, it paused instead of narrowing the investigation. 
           The  full report  retains the initial/final trials, exact candidates and the separate focused-retry follow-up. The separate retry follow-up scored Codex 2/2 in 11.600s versus manager 0/2 in 26.003s: it paused after discovery because it incorrectly treated missing code authorization as blocking focused research. That follow-up is not pooled into this three-task aggregate.  Machine-readable record . 
           Development cases were reused during tuning. Manager usage completeness was not certified for the task without a native worker. Tokens mix models and cached input; they are not dollar costs. Unfinished tasks remain in denominators. No statistical, multi-hour or production benefit is established. 
           Earlier profiles remain available:  v2: manager 4/6 in 176.2s vs Codex 6/6 in 59.0s ;  v1: manager 3/6 in 112.4s vs Codex 6/6 in 62.6s . Fixture, model and tool changes prevent treating these as a controlled trend. 
           Bugs found during live trials 
           Live runs exposed API-key routing, SDK/SQLite thread affinity, invalid scopes, hidden read limits, unhandled turn exhaustion, missing report/check context, prefetch budget starvation and mutable/unstarted-worktree scoring. Failures and partial trials are retained. 
           A separate real Codex repository review found a stale-publication race. A second SQLite connection reproduced it; discovery maps and findings now publish under a writer transaction with a final revision fence. This independent repository review is not a manager benchmark success. 
           Real interaction also returned a manager reply in 2.52s during a delayed worker, delivered policy steering/interruption and restored conversations/messages. These functional checks do not measure recovery rates. 
           Reproduce harness checks 
           python scripts/demo.py --output .omnitrix/demo-new
python scripts/faults.py --output .omnitrix/faults-new
python scripts/benchmark.py --output .omnitrix/benchmark-new
python scripts/check_ui.py 
           Mock decisions use real SQLite, Git and subprocess checks. Nine fault scenarios cover process kills, requirement changes, stale results, repeated verification failure, misleading evidence, lost acknowledgments, external waiting and activity without progress. Browser checks require Playwright/Chromium. 
           Benchmark artifacts retain initial trees, exact candidate revisions, criterion logs, usage, corrections, queries and interventions. Missing measurements remain null. Declared criterion coverage does not measure broader business utility. 
           Multi-hour live comparison 
           Requires  OPENAI_API_KEY , installed Codex dependencies and an isolated development machine. Calls are paid; code authorization applies only to generated fixtures. 
           export OMNITRIX_MODEL=gpt-5.4
python scripts/benchmark.py --live --allow-code-modifications \
  --hours 4 --steps 12 --arm-seconds 1200 --output .omnitrix/live-4h 
           
             Keep fixtures, oracles, worker models and per-arm deadlines identical. Include manager/research usage and all unfinished tasks. 
             Score immutable candidate revisions. Reconcile incomplete turns and external actions before resuming. 
             Use  omnitrix --db PATH status/send/messages  to steer; record every intervention. Hours repeat whole trials and may overrun to finish a pair. 
             Check usage completeness and distinguish an explicit completion claim from a turn simply ending. 
           
           No multi-hour comparative experiment has been completed. Next evidence should use held-out tasks, repeated trials and live interruption faults.  Research quality reports  and the  Kafka investigation  provide separate real-project exploration records.

title: Recovery & operations
text:
One manager owns each SQLite DB. Other processes may inspect state
            or queue commands.
           
           omnitrix run GOAL_ID --steps 50 --hours 4
omnitrix status GOAL_ID
omnitrix messages GOAL_ID
omnitrix send GOAL_ID 'What are you working on?' --id unique-id
 
           Preserve state 
           
            Back up the WAL-consistent DB, adjacent  .sessions.db ,
            instructions, Codex home, repositories/Git metadata, worktrees and
            artifacts together. Use SQLite backup or stop writes before copying.
            Copying only the main DB during WAL writes is unsafe. Preserve paths
            or repair linked worktrees after relocation. Credentials and
            processes must be reestablished; filesystem restoration does not
            restore them.
           
           Reconcile before retrying 
           
            Normal shutdown interrupts work and retains paused/uncertain state.
            SIGKILL cannot clean up. Restart marks running work and in-flight
            sends uncertain; budgets and evidence survive. Ownership uses an OS
            lock, not a stale PID.
           
           
             
               
                 Situation 
                 Action 
               
             
             
               
                 Unknown worker outcome 
                 
                   /reconcile TASK_ID ; inspect exact native
                  thread/turn
                 
               
               
                 Completed code, lost response 
                 Verify the retained candidate without coding again 
               
               
                 Known interrupted/failed turn 
                 Authorize a bounded repair after reconciliation 
               
               
                 Missing native history 
                 Inspect artifacts manually; do not blindly replace work 
               
               
                 Lost delivery acknowledgment 
                 
                   /resolve MESSAGE_ID delivered EVIDENCE  or
                   not_delivered EVIDENCE 
                 
               
               
                 Old question after reconnect 
                 
                  Resume with the actual answer; never reuse an old numeric RPC
                  ID
                 
               
             
           
           
            A missing response does not prove an action failed.
             not_delivered  permits a later explicit resend; it does
            not resend automatically. Native answers remain
             sent_no_ack . Exactly-once execution is not promised.
            SDK research restarts bounded attempts with prior knowledge; pause
            is interrupt/resume, not an OS freeze.
           
           Changes and stalls 
           
            Explicitly accepted policy/goal changes fence affected tasks and
            revoke code authorizations. Keep original mandatory criteria;
            reauthorize and verify current requirements. Unaffected work and
            historical evidence remain.
           
           
            Distinct observations, command/file outcomes and verification
            artifacts count as progress. Tokens, repeated identical events and
            process activity do not reset timers. Waiting does not poll models,
            but wall deadlines still apply. Research/repair budgets persist;
            exhaustion escalates. Inspect activity, messages, research
            runs/queries, external actions and audits.
           
           Nested sandbox limitation 
           
            Codex requires its real owner-only
             /tmp/codex-daemon-<uid>  directory. An outer
            sandbox may mask it with mode 000, preventing nested commands. Use
            the environment-approved route outside that outer sandbox while
            retaining Codex's own sandbox. Never disable sandboxing or weaken
            the reserved directory. Recorded live runs required that route.

title: Omnitrix exploration and exploitation: findings and repair log
Status & limitations
text:
Implemented 
           Area Current behavior 
             Manager Durable conversational session, original criteria, versioned policy and serialized decisions. 
             Workers Real Codex sessions, nonblocking interaction, native steering, durable delivery and restart reconciliation. 
             Research Bounded discovery → falsifiable hypothesis → independent evaluation; reusable evidence and atomic revision-fenced publication. 
             Implementation Explicit authorization, isolated worktrees, independent executable checks, bounded repair and goal audit. 
             UI Password login, persistent sessions, scoped goal creation, heartbeat, task evidence, delivery state, approval diffs and exact-revision criterion coverage. 
             Hosting Tested systemd/Caddy templates. No public live backend; existing Pages site serves recorded experiments. 
           
           Evidence 
           139 tests passed, 1 opt-in live test skipped; ten browser checks passed.  Tests use real SQLite, SDK sessions, Git worktrees and subprocesses with deterministic model decisions. The opt-in Codex test requires live credentials. 
           
             Browser checks cover login, bounded goal creation, approval review, task evidence, delivery recovery, keyboard use, mobile layout and offline snapshot retention. Local validation also restored a password session and displayed an online manager over saved experiment state. 
             Backend regressions cover independent heartbeat during slow replies, stale proposals, concurrent revision changes, exact candidate coverage, duplicate commands and scoped idempotent goal creation. 
             Systemd templates and official Caddy 2.11.7 configuration validated. Local HTTPS verified secure login, CSRF-protected creation and logout with an explicitly trusted temporary CA. 
             scripts/demo.py  demonstrates research → authorization → failed check → repair → audit.  scripts/faults.py  retains nine recovery/fault scenarios. 
           
           Latest complete development trial · unchanged executable criteria System Criteria Time Single Codex 6/6 58.217s Manager 4/6 206.375s 
           No measured architecture advantage.  A separate retry follow-up scored Codex 2/2 in 11.600s versus manager 0/2 in 26.003s; the manager incorrectly treated code authorization as a research blocker. These reused development fixtures do not establish statistical superiority or production value. The  research-judgment report  retains failures and follow-ups separately. 
           Known limits 
           
             Single trusted host, local filesystem and POSIX locks; no distributed ownership or exactly-once guarantee. 
             Uncertain native outcomes may require manual reconciliation. Restarts start in standby rather than blindly repeating actions. 
             Research uses bounded local sources. Exact repeat detection misses paraphrases; citations and hashes do not prove semantic truth or metric freshness. 
             Over-investigation, compound hypotheses and confusing code authorization with permission to research can hide useful narrower defects. Prompt improvements have not eliminated these failures. 
             Verification covers authorized executable criteria; it is not a hostile-code sandbox or proof of unspecified behavior. 
             Provider usage can be incomplete after failed/interrupted calls. Observed tokens across models and caches are not dollar costs. 
             No public host/domain is configured. Target-host TLS issuance, Codex sandbox execution and recovery still require validation. 
           
           Next work 
           Validate on the selected host. Run repeated held-out project tasks and multi-hour interruption experiments. Reduce unnecessary research without weakening citation, authorization or verification gates. 
           API versions 
           openai-agents==0.24.0 ,  @openai/codex-sdk==0.163.0 , inspected Codex App Server 0.159.2 schemas. Both Codex paths use  OPENAI_API_KEY . See  recovery  for nested-sandbox constraints and  deployment  for tested templates.

title: Get started
text:
Omnitrix 
 A persistent engineering manager using the OpenAI Agents SDK, real Codex workers,
and SQLite. It plans bounded research, accepts steering during work, and verifies
explicitly authorized code changes. The manager has  not outperformed a single Codex
worker  in the recorded trials. 
 Install 
 Requires Python 3.11+, Node 20+, Git, and Codex CLI on PATH. Linux/macOS only. 
 python -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e '.[test]'
npm ci
pytest -q
 
 Set  OPENAI_API_KEY  securely; all agents and Codex adapters use it. Never put keys in
goals, files, or the database. Model calls cost money. Without the key, Codex keeps its
existing login configuration.  OMNITRIX_CODEX_PATH  can select the installed CLI. 
 
 
 
 Setting 
 Default 
 
 
 
 
 OMNITRIX_MODEL 
 gpt-4.1 
 
 
 OMNITRIX_CODEX_MODEL 
 gpt-5.3-codex 
 
 
 OMNITRIX_CODEX_HOME 
 .omnitrix/codex-api 
 
 
 Database ( --db PATH  before command) 
 .omnitrix/state.db 
 
 
 
 Use a source/editable install: instructions and Node bridge are repository resources. 
 Run and observe 
 omnitrix create 'Improve service reliability' \
  --criterion 'Verify one bounded improvement' --require-implementation --workspace .
omnitrix chat GOAL_ID
# Another terminal; read-only app and HTML documentation:
omnitrix --db .omnitrix/state.db dashboard
 
 The dashboard defaults to read-only on loopback port 8765. Authenticated control is opt-in.
Use  --require-implementation  for code goals: recommendations alone cannot complete them. 
 
 
 
 Chat command 
 Purpose 
 
 
 
 
 /status ,  /events ,  /run 10 
 Inspect or run bounded decisions 
 
 
 /policy TEXT ,  /accept PROPOSAL_ID 
 Propose and explicitly accept permanent policy 
 
 
 /requirements JSON 
 Add constraints/criteria; originals cannot be removed 
 
 
 /send TASK_ID TEXT 
 Steer a worker 
 
 
 /pause TASK_ID ,  /cancel TASK_ID 
 Interrupt work, retaining state 
 
 
 /answer MESSAGE_ID JSON 
 Answer a worker question 
 
 
 /reconcile TASK_ID 
 Inspect an uncertain native turn 
 
 
 /resolve MESSAGE_ID delivered EVIDENCE 
 Record delivery reconciliation 
 
 
 /quit 
 Save and shut down 
 
 
 
 /policy  replaces the full policy; review before accepting. Requirement JSON accepts
 constraint ,  add_requirements , and  affected_tasks ; omitted task IDs affect all active work.
Changes revoke implementation authorization. Pause interrupts; it is not an OS freeze. 
 omnitrix run GOAL_ID --steps 50 --hours 4
omnitrix send GOAL_ID 'What are you working on?' --id unique-message-id
omnitrix send GOAL_ID 'TASK_ID Check contradictory evidence' --command steer
omnitrix status GOAL_ID
omnitrix messages GOAL_ID
omnitrix knowledge GOAL_ID 'retry'
omnitrix export GOAL_ID > research.json
omnitrix report GOAL_ID --output research.html
 
 One manager owns each DB.  send  queues to that owner; it never starts another manager.
 resume GOAL_ID --steps 5 --message TEXT  restarts bounded work when no owner is running. 
 Agent quality gates 
 Every model entry point receives  instructions/QUALITY_GATES.md  plus its own role
prompt through  omnitrix/prompts.py . The master manager reviews acceptance; the
 AgentBrain  layer maintains evidence and decision quality; discovery maps scope;
research tests hypotheses; evaluation challenges findings; repository workers inspect;
implementation workers explain, validate and prepare operational handoff. Chat reports
these distinctions without turning status questions into new work. 
 New worker/research/evaluation handoffs include a Markdown  quality_report : why the
answer works, sourced charts/diagrams or evidence tables, established-practice fit,
validation and limitations, role-appropriate follow-through, and PASS/RETURN/BLOCKED/N/A
gate outcomes. Research uses validation/invalidation triggers; implementation uses
rollout, monitoring and rollback plans. A PR alone never satisfies acceptance. 
 These are model instructions and review gates, backed by the existing deterministic
source, scope, authorization, revision and executable-check gates. They are not an
automatic semantic grader or a production monitoring service. Old stored handoffs
still load; an absent quality report is unreviewed. New/resumed model invocations load
current prompts; an already-running turn is not retroactively changed. See
 role contracts and review examples . 
 Authorize an implementation 
 A committed Git workspace, explicit authorization and executable checks for every
mandatory criterion are required. Unknown defects/designs use accepted research;
a well-specified bounded change can use the direct contract below. Review
 implementation.json : 
 {
  "objective": "Fix the bounded retry contract",
  "basis": "direct",
  "contract": "Retry only the documented transient error up to the supplied positive attempt limit; preserve all executable acceptance contracts.",
  "allowed_paths": ["src/retry.py"],
  "checks": [{
    "requirement": "EXACT CURRENT MANDATORY CRITERION TEXT",
    "argv": ["/absolute/path/python", "/absolute/path/trusted_check.py"],
    "timeout": 60,
    "failure_kind": "local"
  }],
  "max_attempts": 2,
  "seconds": 300
}
 
 omnitrix authorize GOAL_ID implementation.json --allow-code-modifications
omnitrix resume GOAL_ID --steps 5
 
 For research-backed changes, use  "basis": "research"  (the backward-compatible
default) and  "research_job": "ACCEPTED_RESEARCH_JOB_ID"  instead of  contract .
The supervisor starts a ready direct authorization without a planning round trip,
resumes the native thread for bounded local repairs, independently verifies the
candidate, runs the deterministic audit, and returns once to the manager for the
final evidence review. This route also serves as a bounded, explicitly authorized
implementation experiment; research-only campaigns cannot use it. 
 Manager decisions receive one current snapshot with complete criteria, recent
history and durable dialogue. Older original reports remain available through
 recall_history / recall_artifact ; state snapshots are not replayed as conversation.
Research/evaluation receives the current acceptance criteria and separates blocking
questions from nonblocking uncertainties. Independent read-only investigations can
use  research_batch  with 2..3 plans and an  independence_reason ; all saved scope,
revision, role-run, dollar and cancellation limits still apply. 
 Every mandatory criterion needs an executable check.  failure_kind: "assumption" 
returns failures to research. External oracles are hashed;  OMNITRIX_CANDIDATE  identifies
the clean candidate worktree. Commands are trusted local processes, not a hostile-code
sandbox; provider credentials are removed. Authorization permits bounded worktree edits,
never deployments, destructive operations, merges or pushes. 
 Compare the single worker, research-first manager and adaptive route on identical
fixture contracts with  python scripts/benchmark.py --trials 2 --arms single manager adaptive --output .omnitrix/comparison-NEW . Add  --live --allow-code-modifications 
for real model usage. Reports separate coordinator, research, coding and verification
timings, model/token metadata and independently scored outcomes. These small fixtures
test orchestration; they cannot establish production or architecture superiority.

 Durable research campaigns 
 Create a fresh goal for a pinned local clone, then start a read-only investigation
with persistent time, decision, role-run and dollar limits: 
 omnitrix create 'Find system inefficiencies and compare falsifiable explanations' \
  --criterion 'Distinguish code mechanisms, measured impact and missing data' \
  --workspace /absolute/path/to/pinned-repository
omnitrix --db .omnitrix/state.db campaign GOAL_ID \
  --days 3 --decisions 1000 --research-runs 2000 --dollars 25
# After a process restart: reuse the same DB and goal, without new limits.
omnitrix --db .omnitrix/state.db campaign GOAL_ID
# Inspect or pause from another terminal.
omnitrix --db .omnitrix/state.db status GOAL_ID
omnitrix --db .omnitrix/state.db campaign GOAL_ID --pause
 
 Each campaign is capped at $25. Standard-tier GPT-4.1 requests reserve maximum
cost before inference; lost responses retain that reservation. Native workers,
hosted tools, code changes and external PRs are disabled for these campaigns.
The HTML checkpoint includes evidence, decisions, spending and remaining coverage.
Register local exported logs/CSV with repeatable  --evidence workspace/relative/path ;
record workload and measurement-window context alongside them. See the
 campaign and tracking guide  for pricing, recovery, explicit
continuation after a pause, and the limits of the current Kafka experiment.

 Research quality evaluation and self-audit 
 The  HTML findings and repair log  records baseline
failures, changes, actual live outcomes, and unresolved limitations. Its source is
 docs/research-quality.json ; per-goal HTML includes decisions, evidence, queries,
evaluations and measured model usage. Source/model text is escaped, never executed.
Each issue retains dated observations, fixes, tests and regressions. Latest run
summaries coexist with an append-only experiment history, including model costs
and coverage where available. A fixed guard is distinguished from improved live
research behavior; unresolved failures remain visible. 
 # Scripted tool/harness checks: these do not measure model reasoning.
python scripts/research_eval.py --harness-only --output .omnitrix/eval-harness-NEW
# Paid autonomous discovery: competing clues and a negative control, scored outside the workspace.
python scripts/research_eval.py --live --output .omnitrix/eval-live-NEW --log docs/research-quality.json
# Real Omnitrix source, seeded failing probes, autonomous triage and authorized Codex repair.
python scripts/self_audit.py --allow-code-modifications --output .omnitrix/self-audit-NEW --log docs/research-quality.json
 
 Use new output directories.  --live  needs API credentials and API network access.
The self-audit clones the selected committed revision locally, retains every
candidate, and limits worker changes to  omnitrix/research.py ; independent oracles
live outside the candidate. It performs no merge, push or PR publication. Running
the script through an outer sandbox that masks Codex's daemon socket can block
worker shells; keep Codex's own sandbox enabled when using a supported execution route. 
 Synthetic scoring measures observable research behavior, with explicitly reported
lexical target matching. It is not proof of causal correctness or generalization
to large public repositories. The self-audit probes are human-authored known
failures: successful triage/repair is separate from autonomous issue discovery.
The research evaluator exits 0 only when every checkpoint passes, 1 for behavioral
failures (or no trials), and 2 for blocked/error runs. A completed agent conversation
does not by itself pass the evaluation.
